title: Testing on hardware the project does not own
alt: A tester runs the image, sends the report, and CI checks it before it appears on the hardware-reports page.
text: Tester's machine: Tester image or macOS bundle (published per release), GPU rows and twins (every twin against the CPU), Report JSON (facts, verdicts, digest).
Project: check-hardware-reports.py (schema, verdicts, digest), Hardware reports page (generate-hardware-reports.py).
Tester image or macOS bundle → GPU rows and twins (run) → Report JSON (write) → check-hardware-reports.py (sent back) → Hardware reports page (make docs-fragments-write).

Scenario 1, One report: A tester's run becomes a row on the hardware-reports page. The image probes the GPU and runs every row it can. Each twin is compared with the CPU; the report records the verdicts. The tester sends the report; CI checks its schema and digest. The page lists the report with its backend and verdict.
The report carries a digest of its own content, so an edited report fails the check.
